title: Preparation of the intact rodent organ of Corti for RNAscope and immunolabeling
author: Reijntjes, Breitzler, et al.
materials: RNAscope Multiplex Fluorescent Reagent Kit v2

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Assemble dissecting tools, make all required solutions (ice‑cold PBS, 4 % PFA, 0.4 % PFA, external or RNA‑preservation solutions) in advance, and ensure access to dissecting microscope, fluorescence microscope and computer workstations.

steps.title: Anesthetize and decapitate mouse
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia according to institutional approval, confirm depth by absence of withdrawal reflexes, then decapitate the mouse with surgical scissors.

steps.title: Expose inner ear
steps.instruction: Bisect the skull and palate sagittally with surgical scissors, taking care not to damage the temporal bone; remove the brain with scissors or a spatula to reveal the inner ear embedded in each temporal bone.

steps.title: Dissect temporal bone
steps.instruction: Excise the sections of temporal bone containing the inner ear (identified by the semicircular canals) with surgical scissors and place them in a 5‑cm plastic petri dish containing ice‑cold PBS. Alternatives: ice‑cold 4 % PFA, 0.4 % PFA at 20‑22 °C, appropriate external solution, or RNA‑preservation solution (use a fume hood when handling PFA).

steps.title: Secure inner ear in dish
steps.instruction: Under a dissecting microscope, position a pair of forceps around the inner ear at the cochlea‑semicircular canal junction and press the forceps and dish down to hold the temporal bone firmly without squeezing the inner ear.

steps.title: Release inner ear from bone
steps.instruction: Use blunt forceps to gently detach the inner ear from the temporal bone and auditory bulla.

steps.title: Transfer to fresh solution
steps.instruction: Move the isolated inner ear to a new 5‑cm dish containing fresh ice‑cold PBS (or ice‑cold/room‑temperature 4 % or 0.4 % PFA, external solution, or RNA‑preservation solution) and repeat the securing and release steps for the second ear so both are in the same dish.

steps.title: Create apical access hole
steps.instruction: With one blade of the forceps, gently scrape and chip a small hole in the bone over the apical turn of the cochlea large enough to expose the apical turn while avoiding damage to the lateral wall or organ of Corti.

steps.title: Fix inner ears
steps.instruction: Transfer both inner ears to ice‑cold 4 % PFA in 5‑ or 15‑mL plastic centrifuge tubes and fix for 30 min to 3 h (typical start 1 h; for RNAscope fix 1 h at room temperature followed by 15 min on ice). Adjust fixation time based on primary‑antibody requirements.

steps.title: Prepare for organ isolation
steps.instruction: After fixation, place the inner ears into a dissecting dish with fresh ice‑cold PBS (or the appropriate solution) for subsequent organ of Corti isolation.

steps.title: Remove bone over organ
steps.instruction: Hold the inner ear with forceps as before; use a second pair of forceps to enlarge the apical hole, gradually removing bone until all cochlear turns and the most basal hook are exposed.

steps.title: Peel lateral wall
steps.instruction: Using fine forceps, pinch the lateral wall at the apical turn and unwind it away from the organ of Corti, proceeding toward basal turns while avoiding damage.

steps.title: Detach basal turn
steps.instruction: Insert one blade of fine forceps beneath the basal hook and gently push upward to separate the basal turn (with underlying bone) from the modiolus; work slowly.

steps.title: Release organ from modiolus
steps.instruction: Insert a fine‑forceps blade between the apical turn and the modiolus, gently push upward to free the organ of Corti; continue around each turn until the entire organ is released. Use a small dissecting knife or microscissors if central spiral‑ganglion projections impede release; the organ may be isolated in multiple pieces if necessary.

steps.title: Remove tectorial membrane
steps.instruction: Hold the organ of Corti with one fine‑forceps pair, pinch the tectorial membrane at the apical turn with a second pair, and unwind it away from the organ.

steps.title: Transfer organ to well
steps.instruction: Clear excess bone and place the isolated organ(s) of Corti into a 24‑well cell‑culture plate (300–400 µL solution per well; 1–4 organs per well) or onto microscope slides within a circle‑shaped hydrophobic barrier for RNAscope. Transfer gently with fine forceps; exchange solutions with a 1000 µL micropipettor without disturbing the samples.

steps.title: Block and permeabilize
steps.instruction: Incubate samples in blocking buffer (500–1000 µL per well) for at least 1 h at room temperature. Samples may be stored in blocking buffer at 4 °C for days to weeks (seal with parafilm) without loss of immunoreactivity.

steps.title: Remove blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL micropipettor, aspirate the blocking buffer from each well.

steps.title: Add primary antibody
steps.instruction: Add primary antibody diluted to the appropriate concentration in fresh blocking buffer.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the organs of Corti in primary antibody solution for at least 4 h up to 48 h at room temperature (incubation at 4 °C is also acceptable).

steps.title: Rinse with PBT
steps.instruction: Rinse samples three times with PBT, each wash lasting 10 min at room temperature. Samples may be stored in PBT at 4 °C if needed.

steps.title: Add secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove PBT and add secondary antibody diluted to the appropriate concentration in blocking buffer.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate in secondary antibody solution for at least 4 h up to 24 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Final washes
steps.instruction: Rinse samples three times with PBT for 10 min each, then once with PBS at room temperature.

description: Timing: 2 h Very little preparation is necessary. Necessary reagents should be made in advance. Dissecting equipment should be assembled. Access to necessary microscopes and computer workplaces should be secured. (See details provided in the materials and equipment section below).Note: This protocol has been used to isolate the sensory epithelium of various rodents (e.g., Barone et al. 2019), including aged rodents. The protocol has been adapted for use on the isolated vestibular sensory epithelia (e.g., Sadeghi et al. 2014, Schuth et al. 2014, Greguske et al. 2021).
